This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH-5 2.
The petition averments are briefly stated as follows:

That on 01.09.2022 at about 10.00 p.m. petitioner was riding scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-JU-8412 near Magadi Road Toll Gate, West of Chord Road, Vijayanagar,
Bengaluru, a car bearing Reg. No.KA-50-MB-3148 came in opposite direction at high speed and dashed against the said scooter, as a result of this impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Madhu Hospital, thereafter shifted to HAL Hospital for treatment.

3. Petitioner submitted that at the time of accident, he was aged about 47 years, doing Technician work at HAL and drawing salary of Rs.50,000/- p.m. due to the accidental injuries, he could not attend his duty and not able to daily activities and depending on others.
SCCH-5 With regard to accident, case registered in crime No.112/2022 against the driver of the said Car before the Vijayanagar Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is owner of the offending car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.

4. On service of notice, respondent No.1 being the insurer has appeared through counsel appeared and filed written statement and contended that, alleged accident has taken place on 01.09.2022 and claim petition has been filed on 05.07.2023 i.e., after 10 months 5 days from the date of occurrence of the accident and it has not been filed within the time limit as per provisions under Sec.166(3) of M . V . A c t . F u r t h e r s u b m i t t e d t h a t , i t h a s S C C H - 5 i s s u e d p o l i c y b e a r i n g No.OG-23-9910-1825-00020965 commencing from 16.06.2022 to 15.06.2025 and liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.1 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134 and Sec.159 of M.V.Act.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is entitled to seek protection under Sec.147 and 150 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive.

Accordingly prays to Venktesh Murthy vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167345888/
2 dismiss the petition.

5. Based on above pleadings of the parties following issues are framed:

::ISSUES::
1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the road SCCH-5 traffic accident occurred on 01.09.2022 at about 10.00 p.m. near Magadi Road, Toll Gate, West of Chord Road, Vijayanagar, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02- JU-8412?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
6.

In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1, examined Dr.B.Ramesh,
Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2, Manager (HR) at Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd., is examined as PW-3 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.27.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
SCCH-5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating petition averments.

Inorder to prove rash and negligent driving and compensation the petitioner got marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.3, copy of criminal case order sheet as Ex.P.4, copy of crime detail form as Ex.P.5, copy of Sec.133 notice as Ex.P.6, copy of reply as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.8, copy of B Extract as Ex.P.10.
9.
During the cross examination of P.W-1 nothing is elicited to discard manner of accident, and involvement of offending vehicle.

On perusal of evidence SCCH-5 of PW-1 and documents marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the accident dated 01.09.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, except filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and to Venktesh Murthy vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167345888/
3 discard the evidence of PW-1.

sentences.text:
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 01.09.2022 at about 10.00 p.m.
when he was riding scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-02-JU- 8412 near Magadi Road Toll Gate, West of Chord Road, Vijayanagara, Bengaluru.
11.
The police papers speaks that the very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the Car SCCH-5 bearing Reg. No.KA-50-MB-3148.
Under such circumstances, considering the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left leg both bone comminuted fracture, left humerus fracture tuberosity comminuted, for the said injuries he underwent internal fixation of left tibia and left fracture tuberosity of humerus, later underwent implant removal.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.9, copy of health card as Ex.P.11, medical bills for Rs.35,495/-.
13.

To substantiate the nature of the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner, he has SCCH-5 examined Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW-2 and marked OPD Record as Ex.P.17 and X-ray Films as Ex.P.18.
PW-2 has assessed permanent physical disability of 20% of left lower limb, 18% of left upper limb, which is 15.3% of whole body disability.
In the cross-examination PW-2 deposed that, he is not a treated Doctor and he has not obtained any opinion from treated Doctor and he has seen only discharge summary.
Further deposed that, he is not member of District Medical Board.
Further deposed that, now the fractures are united and implants are removed.

14. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 46 years, in this regard petitioner has produced and marked copy of aadhar card as Ex.P.13, wherein date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.06.1976 and the alleged accident was occurred on 01.09.2022.
SCCH-5
Accordingly relying on Ex.P.13, his age is considered about 46 years as on the date of accident.
15. Petitioner was working as Technician and drawing salary of Rs.50,000/- p.m. in HAL Company.
To prove the same, he has furnished salary slip for the month of December 2024 as Ex.P.19.

In this regard petitioner has examined Manager (HR) at HAL as PW-3 who got marked payslips as Ex.P.20,
copy of fitness certificate as Ex.P.21, copy of leave letter as Ex.P.22, copy of acknowledgment as Ex.P.23, copy of attendance sheet as Ex.P.24, copy of performance memo individual as Ex.P.25,
copy of ID card as Ex.P.26 and copy of SB account statement as Ex.P.27.
As per the version of P.W- 3 the petitioner was on leave from 02.03.2022 to 30.11.2022 on account of medical treatment due to accidental injuries.
As per Ex.P.19 petitioner was on 90 SCCH-5 days leave from 02.03.2022 to 30.11.2022 out of said leave only 17 days leave is leave without pay.
The date of accident is on 01.09.2022 at 10.00 p.m.
As per Ex.P.19 the total salary of petitioner is Rs.83,666/- and if same is taken into consideration per day salary of petitioner is 2,789/-.
Hence petitioner is entitled for loss of pay of Rs.47,413/-.

As per cross examination version of P.W-3 petitioner is continuing in his Venktesh Murthy vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 30 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167345888/
4 service after the road traffic accident.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination PW-1 deposed that, before the accident he was drawing salary of Rs.60,000/- and now also he is drawing Rs.60,000/- as salary.
Under such circumstances, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income on account of disability.
16. The petitioner has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.16 for a sum of Rs.35,495/-.
As per SCCH-5 cross examination version of P.W-1 and P.W-3 petitioner is entitled for medical reimbursement.
It is pertinent to note that petitioner produced medical bills for the year 2023 and 2024 except Sl.No.6 and 7.
this shows that petitioner reimbursed medical bills from the date of accident till his discharge from the hospital.
During the cross examination of P.W-1 he stated that he can produce document to show non reimbursement of medical bills but not produced the same before court.
As contended by the respondent the Sl.No.2,8 to 10,12,15 to 19 are xerox copies.

Sl.No.
3 to 7 are the bills which do not contain the seal, name of the Doctor and petitioner not produced scan pay receipts hence petitioner is not entitled for the said bills.
On perusal of Ex.P.16 the petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,092/- towards medical expenses.
SCCH-5 17

. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl
. No .

Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Pain and sufferings 25,000-00 2. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,000-00 attendant charges 3.
Medical Expenses 6,092-00 4. Loss of amenities in life 15,000-00

Accordingly this Tribunal hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.61,092/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

19. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.OG-23- 9910-1825-00020965 which is valid for the period from 16.06.2022 to 15.06.2025, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.09.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of SCCH-5 accident,
insurance policy was in force.
Hence respondent No.1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
For these reasons Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

20. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.61,092/- (Rupees sixty one thousand ninety two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire amount through e-payment directly to his account SCCH-5 on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
